message.content: Pandas belong to the order Carnivora, but they diverged from other carnivores early on. Their lineage split from the common ancestor of bears around 20–25 million years ago. Over time, they evolved distinct traits—such as a specialized wrist bone that acts like a thumb—to adapt to their bamboo‑based diet. This adaptation allowed them to thrive in forested habitats across Asia. The giant panda’s unique evolutionary path has made it one of the most iconic symbols of conservation worldwide.
